rules.title: Governance Specification vs Operational Ledger
statement: Governance specifications describe intended registry structure.
Operational ledgers record the current canonical state.
Specifications SHALL NEVER serve as operational authority once a live ledger exists.
Operational ledgers SHALL NOT contain proposal metadata.
Proposal history SHALL remain in governance history archives.

rules.title: Governance-First Execution Gate
statement: While any tier-0 or blocker governance task in the live Program Task Registry remains active, planned, or blocked, no new non-governance program work SHALL be initiated.
During this gate, admissible work is limited to governance closure, governance debt reduction, governance routing repair, and textbook synchronization required by those governance changes.
Department, theorem, bridge, simulation, and application expansion work SHALL remain frozen until the governance gate is explicitly lifted in the live Program Task Registry.

rules.title: Induction Registry and Queue Requirement
statement: Every new induction SHALL create or update a canonical induction record in registry/induction_registry.json.
Every new induction SHALL also be entered into governance/live/induction_queue.json before it may be cited as active program work.
An induction lacking both a registry record and a queue entry SHALL be treated as ungoverned and may not be used for promotion, dependency closure, or downstream planning.

rules.title: Department SSOT Authority Separation
statement: Design authority and execution authority are intentionally separated.
Department SSOTs SHALL be parsed before any department-owned modification.
Department SSOTs are mandatory for department-owned modification activities.
Department SSOTs define design intent, while governed registries, validators, and audit contracts define executable state.

rules.title: Governed Task Commit Closeout Requirement
statement: Every governed task that changes repository state SHALL end with an intentional Git commit before task closeout.
The commit SHALL be created only after required validation and textbook synchronization are complete.
The commit SHALL cover the task-scoped governed delta rather than unrelated worktree residue.
If unrelated dirty state prevents an isolated task-scoped commit, the task SHALL remain open and the blocker SHALL be recorded explicitly in the closeout report or governance ledger.
Read-only audit tasks are exempt because they do not modify governed state.

notes: This constitution file defines the live-ledger separation rule introduced by MPF_GOV_LIVE_LEDGER_TRANSITION_001.
Historical proposal artifacts remain preserved under governance/specifications/ and their original locations until repository-wide reference cleanup is complete.
The governance-first execution gate introduced on 2026-07-01 temporarily makes governance closure the only admissible program lane until live governance sections are satisfied.
Department SSOT authority is split from execution authority: design intent comes from Department SSOTs, while runtime truth comes from governed registries and validators.

Governed change tasks now require a task-scoped Git commit after validation and textbook synchronization; if the commit cannot be isolated safely, the task stays open and the blocker must be recorded.
